tools.name: session_status
tools.description: Check whether you are signed in to Juicyway (loads your profile via GET /me). Call before other tools; if this fails, use start_browser_auth.

tools.name: bank_transfer
tools.description: Bank transfer / payout flow for Juicyway.

tools.name: create_payout
tools.description: Create a bank payout/transfer. Prefill beneficiary from session when possible. Always emit_display preview before running.

tools.name: start_browser_auth
tools.description: Open the site sign-in only when needed. If the saved session is still valid, this tool returns success immediately and does not open the viewer. Call session_status first. Use force_reconnect only when the user explicitly wants to wipe the saved cookie and sign in again (destructive).

tools.name: get_network_identity
tools.description: Where this user's requests to the site leave from (a VPN country, the server, or the app's default) and which browser they present. Read-only.

tools.name: set_network_identity
tools.description: Choose where this user's requests to the site leave from and which browser they present, only when the user asks (e.g. 'connect through Nigeria', 'use my own user agent'). Sites may ask the user to sign in again when this changes. reset=true goes back to how they signed in.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "start_browser_auth" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "start_browser_auth" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
